Requirement (Yêu cầu): 5 BERT models: tiny, mini, small, medium, base
What the paper / original code does: Paper uses 24 BERT checkpoints incl. these five (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 3 red stars)
What we did: Five Google checkpoints L-2_H-128, L-4_H-256, L-4_H-512, L-8_H-512, L-12_H-768
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Same lr and epochs for every model
What the paper / original code does: Paper: lr not stated (UNVERIFIED); fixed steps (Sec. 3.4)
What we did: lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, batch 128 for all 27 runs; training_args.bin of every run identical apart from seed and max_steps
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): lr was chosen from two values after 8 steps (losses near chance, see D5); not tuned per model

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Fixed eval set: 1,000 queries, pool 100,000, 256 negatives, num_repeat 5
What the paper / original code does: Original evaluate.py defaults: pool 1,000,000, repeat 10, all valid dev queries (DRScale_repo/evaluate.py:123-128)
What we did: 1,000 queries (1,086 pairs), pool 100,000, 256 negatives, 5 repeats
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Smaller than the repo defaults; see C10

Requirement (Yêu cầu): 3 seeds
What the paper / original code does: Paper: number of seeds not stated (UNVERIFIED)
What we did: Seeds 42/43/44 for all 9 configurations (27 runs)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Data sweep at 5 points 2,500…40,000 on L-4_H-512_A-8
What the paper / original code does: Paper sweeps up to ~500K on BERT-Base (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 4)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): 2-param log-regression fit and 3-param fit with boundary check
What we did: 2-param OLS on log–log; 3-param curve_fit with bounds; recomputation reproduces SUMMARY (all six SUMMARY values reproduce to the printed precision); unbounded refit gives the same optimum
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): 3-param data exponent is not stable (D6 / Sec. 5)

Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Score = inner product; no temperature / normalisation stated
What we did: Plain dot product; no L2 normalisation; no temperature
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Loss: contrastive CE with random and in-batch negatives, 256 negatives per step
What the paper / original code does: Softmax CE over positive + sampled negatives
What we did: Per batch: 256 random corpus passages shared by all queries; K = 1+256 = 257; mean CE. Other queries' positives are not added as negatives (code level). Whether the paper's 'in-batch' means the same is UNVERIFIED.
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Low

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Optimisation length
What we did: 3 epochs → 60 / 120 / 237 / 471 / 939 steps for D = 2,500…40,000 (checkpoint-N dirs, trainer_state.json)
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Models are far from converged (F8); the data sweep confounds D with number of steps, the model sweep is a 237-step regime. Exponents are regime-specific and not comparable with the paper.

Requirement (Yêu cầu): lr, batch size, optimiser, max lengths
What the paper / original code does: Paper silent (UNVERIFIED). Repo defaults: lr 5e-6, 80 epochs, batch 128, max query 25, max doc 180 (DRScale_repo/training_arguments.py:47-54,71-72)
What we did: lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, batch 128, AdamW (wd 0.001), linear decay, warmup 10, clip 1.0, bf16, max query 25 (eval 32), max doc 180
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Higher lr is needed for a 60–939-step schedule; not tuned per model

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Metric: contrastive entropy = NLL of the positive among 1+256 candidates
What the paper / original code does: −log softmax; the paper calls it 'contrastive entropy'; the repo function is named contrastive_perplexity but returns the mean NLL (no exp)
What we did: Same NLL (nats). Original plots/SUMMARY call it 'Contrastive Perplexity' [OLD-LABEL]; values 0.1581–0.7265 are < 1, impossible for a perplexity. Chance level ln(257) = 5.549
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Naming only; all package figures/tables relabelled 'contrastive entropy (NLL, nats)'

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Evaluation set and negatives
What the paper / original code does: ~7,000 dev queries (Sec. 3.3); 256 negatives and a 100,000-passage sub-corpus in the metric study (Sec. 3.5); number of dev queries/repeats in the main figures not stated (UNVERIFIED)
What we did: First 1,000 dev.small queries by qid; pool 100,000; 5 repeats; final-model evaluation
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Slightly noisier and mildly biased subset (D7). SUMMARY's claim that the paper uses a 1,000,000 pool is wrong: that is the repo default (DRScale_repo/evaluate.py:128), not stated in the paper

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Which checkpoint is reported
What the paper / original code does: Best test loss over training, no early stopping
What we did: Final checkpoint after the last step
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Slightly pessimistic if loss rose at the end; training loss was still falling (F8)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): N = non-embedding parameters
What we did: Counts incl. unused BERT pooler and the projection layer (repo definition). In units of 2^20 they are 0.5, 3.3, 12.7, 24.7, 82.2 M, equal to the paper's Fig. 6 labels
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): x-axis uses 10^6 units, so numbers differ by 4.8% from the paper's labels; same models

Requirement (Yêu cầu): D = number of annotated query–passage pairs
What we did: (qid, pid) pairs
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Data sweep model and range
What we did: BERT-Small; 2,500–40,000 pairs
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Different regime; exponent β not comparable

What we did: Not reproduced (not requested)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Full MS MARCO corpus
What we did: 8,326,970 passages (94.18%; file truncated, last line cut)
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Low (see D8)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Mixed precision
What we did: bf16 training, fp32 evaluation
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Unknown effect; same for all models

Requirement (Yêu cầu): No query leakage between train and evaluation
What we did: Train qids ∩ dev qids = 0; train-qrels qids ∩ the 1,000 eval qids = 0; exact lower-cased query text overlap = 0. (52 eval positive PASSAGES also appear as train positives for other queries: standard in MS MARCO, informational)
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

Requirement (Yêu cầu): How the D pairs are chosen
What we did: Seeded shuffle of all 529,440 unique pairs, first D taken: nested across D within a seed; across seeds the 10,000-pair subsets overlap 203–207 pairs (≈189 expected by chance), i.e. independent
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Models at the same seed see the same data (paired design)

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Seed control (init, data order, negatives, eval)
What we did: Seed sets python/numpy/torch RNG: projection init differs across seeds (checked), data shuffle and training negatives differ; evaluation seed is fixed to 1 for every model
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Fair comparison, but SD excludes evaluation-sampling noise

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Same evaluation negatives for all models
What we did: set_seed(1) immediately before sampling; rebuilding the pool twice gives identical IDs (sha1 f965e175b62f…). Not logged per run, so shown by code + replication, not observed in the original runs
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Paired comparison; low noise in differences between models

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Hyper-parameters not tuned per model; lr choice
What we did: lr picked from {5e-5, 1e-4} after 8 steps; the losses were 5.4256 and 4.9708, close to chance (5.549), so the evidence for the choice is weak
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Larger models may be under-tuned; equal settings keep the comparison fair

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Train loss vs eval loss comparable (to discuss over-fitting)?
What we did: Not like-for-like: train loss is a running mean over the whole run (train_output.training_loss), in train mode (dropout), bf16, on seen pairs; eval is final model, eval mode, fp32, held-out queries. Same K = 257 and same formula only. Last-window train loss (small: 0.0555) is far below dev loss (0.2345) but this is not evidence of over-fitting
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): No 'over-fitting' claim allowed

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Bias of 'first 1,000 queries by qid'
What we did: Subset is qids ≤ 249,792 (dev max 1,102,400); mean query length 5.30 vs 6.03 words for the remaining dev queries; positives per query 1.086 vs 1.062
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Mild; shifts absolute levels, not the ranking of models

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Effect of truncated corpus
What we did: Missing passages are the highest ids (5.82%). 3,311 of 532,751 unique train pairs (0.62%) and 3,067 queries lose all positives; their queries are slightly shorter (5.74 vs 5.97 words). Dev loses no pair. Negatives come from ids 0…8,326,969. Whether ids carry topical order is UNVERIFIED
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): Low

Requirement (Yêu cầu): Provenance of early seed-42 runs
What we did: Six JSON files (tiny…medium, D=2,500, 5,000 at seed 42) have no seed field and their log was overwritten; training_args.bin of those checkpoints shows seed 42, lr 1e-4, bf16, warmup 10, batch 128, 3 epochs, the same as all other runs
Impact on conclusions (Ảnh hưởng): None

What we did: All 27 JSON values equal results.csv (max diff 0.0e+00); recomputed means/SD equal results_summary.csv (max diff 3.3e-05, rounding)
